sites.source: https://cpw.state.co.us/state-wildlife-areas/clear-creek-reservoir-swa and the CPW SWA map give no site count; the stored ~20 came from RV Life/Campendium via the note, so it is cleared. Read 2026-10-27

note: CPW State Wildlife Area campground at the west (inlet) end of Clear Creek Reservoir, ~13 mi N of Buena Vista: US-24 to County Road 390, then ~2 mi of maintained gravel along the north shore. Camping only in the designated campground; fires only in containment structures there. Boat ramp on the north shore. Open flats at the Clear Creek inlet; some drive-in RV sites sit right along Clear Creek (creekside), reservoir a short walk east. --Claude
summary: CPW SWA page + map: camping allowed in designated areas only, with one campground (tent symbol + restroom) at the west end; license or SWA pass for everyone 16+ (now in fees.note); no camping fee posted. Confirmed $0; cleared the directory-only site count of 20. Not stated: road surface (no 4WD wording), site count, lengths, season, booking. Note trimmed (RV Life line and field facts dropped).
flags: Designated sites confirmed: CPW's restrictions read 'A. Camping allowed in designated areas only. B. Fires allowed within a containment structure in designated camping areas', and the CPW map marks a Campground (with restroom and info board) at the west end of the reservoir. Qualifies as agency-designated SWA camping.

Access: CPW map says 'From Buena Vista, go 13 miles north on Highway 24 to County Road 390, then 1/2 mile west' (to the SWA; the campground is ~1.7 mi further west by the map). No 4WD or high-clearance wording anywhere; road surface not stated by CPW.

Waterfront lead (stored 'creekside'): OSM's campground polygon reaches Clear Creek (6 m) just above the inlet and sits 151 m from the mapped reservoir edge; the pin is 222 m from the creek and 405 m from the reservoir (pin ~117 m from the polygon centre, OK). Imagery (z18): open sagebrush flats with gravel loops; the SE pull-outs sit under conifers ~10-30 m from Clear Creek, the rest of the loops 100 m+ away. Creekside looks supportable for the SE sites; the reservoir is not in view from them.
Open now; no CPW alerts for the SWA.
